rule: If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. ... Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, ...) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. ... Call on a computed receiver (... `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member`
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. `this("rex")` is a constructor delegation listed with the superclass-constructor rule (`: this(...)`), callee the class's own <init>. `super.speak()` with the superclass in the scan names Animal#speak (the `.member` form is only for a superclass outside the scan). `eat` is defined only on Animal, so both `this.eat()` and bare `eat()` are Animal#eat; `speak` is overridden in Dog, so `this.speak()` is Dog#speak. `@Override` is an annotation, not a call. Inside Animal#eat the bare `speak()` names the enclosing type's member Animal#speak (static ID; virtual dispatch is not expanded for Java).
